name: Basilica Julia
type: archaeological site; civil basilica; destroyed building or structure
text: The Basilica Julia (Italian: Basilica Giulia) was a civil basilica in the Roman Forum. Construction began under Julius Caesar in 46 BC and was completed by Augustus, who ultimately dedicated the basilica to Gaius and Lucius Caesar in 12 AD. It served as the headquarters for the centumviri, a judicial court that primarily dealt with matters of inheritance.

depictions.name: Basilica Giulia
depictions.text: The Basilica Julia (Italian: Basilica Giulia) is a structure that once stood in the Roman Forum. It was a large, ornate public building used for meetings and other official business during the early Roman Empire.
